xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4331: Spike: `npx @overdeck/core` and Session Vault resume on native Windows

plan.title: Spike: `npx @overdeck/core` and Session Vault resume on native Windows
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: Nobody has verified that npx @overdeck/core or the standalone pan vault B-flow (join → list → resume, with PAN-4329 code apply) works on native Windows or WSL2, yet the operator's case is to continue a Linux conversation after dual-booting into Windows. pan vault is not in the published 0.63.0, and Herdr likely does not run on Windows.
narratives.Proposal: Build a reproducible windows-smoke GitHub Actions workflow: pack the branch-HEAD tarball exactly as release.yml does, build a Linux fixture vault (saved Claude Code conversation plus uncommitted/unpushed code), run a probe on windows-2022 under pwsh and Git Bash (steps 1a-4f) and in WSL2 (5a plus the B-flow), and summarize the per-step results into a markdown table with verbatim errors. Post the table on #4331, file one issue per blocking root cause, update PAN-3762 NFR-9, and add Windows sections to docs/SESSION-VAULT.md and configuration/session-vault.mdx that state only what the run verified.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Fixing any failure the spike finds (vault, dashboard, Herdr, resume spawn, command quoting); no changes under src/.
- Making Herdr or tmux run on Windows.
- Testing on Windows 11, on a local VM, or a real dual-boot.
- Adding windows-smoke to ci.yml or making it a required check.
- Using any Claude or Anthropic credentials in CI.
- Testing a WSL cwd under /mnt/c, the Electron desktop app (#531), Codex resume on Windows, or the PAN-4293 sign-in flow.
- Creating configuration/anywhere-sign-in.mdx (owned by PAN-4293).

autoDecisions.summary: Run the spike on GitHub-hosted windows-2022 runners instead of a Windows 11 VM.
autoDecisions.rationale: The only local VM (win11-snapcam) has no disk image (~/VMs is empty) and auto mode has no operator to drive a VM; the repo is public so hosted minutes are free, and release.yml already uses Windows runners. Docs name the real environment and never claim Windows 11.

autoDecisions.summary: Test the npm-packed branch-HEAD tarball, plus two rows against published @overdeck/core@latest.
autoDecisions.rationale: pan vault (PAN-2609) and code apply (PAN-4329) landed after v0.63.0, so the published package cannot run the B-flow; packing with bun install --frozen-lockfile, bun run build, npm pack --ignore-scripts reproduces release.yml.

autoDecisions.summary: Run the native probe under both pwsh and Git Bash.
autoDecisions.rationale: pwsh has no HOME (USERPROFILE path) while Git Bash exports a POSIX-style HOME; the issue asks specifically about USERPROFILE/HOME resolution.

autoDecisions.summary: Put the user-facing Windows section in configuration/session-vault.mdx instead of configuration/anywhere-sign-in.mdx.
autoDecisions.rationale: anywhere-sign-in.mdx does not exist; PAN-4293 owns creating it, and session-vault.mdx is the existing user page for the B-flow.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep windows-smoke as a workflow_dispatch plus paths-filtered push workflow after the spike.
autoDecisions.rationale: Filed blocker issues need a way to prove their fix; the paths filter keeps it off normal CI.

autoDecisions.summary: Join the fixture vault with a fixed test passphrase and a local bare git repo backend.
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids parsing the recovery phrase from stdout, exercises a real git backend with a Windows path, and needs no secrets because the vault is throwaway.

items.title: Add the Linux fixture builder scripts/windows-smoke/make-fixture.sh

verify_commands: gh run view <windows-smoke run id> --log (job fixture)
expected_outputs: the fixture job exits 0 and uploads the "fixture" artifact with origin.git, vault.git, passphrase.txt and fixture.json

narrative.Action: Implement PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-4331.md work item W1 exactly: a bash script (set -euo pipefail) taking one output dir OUT, using an isolated HOME=$OUT/home and OVERDECK_HOME=$OUT/home/.overdeck, that builds a bare origin.git with one pushed commit (README.md, lf.txt), a clone carrying an unpushed commit "fixture: unpushed commit", a modified lf.txt, a CRLF crlf.txt, an executable run.sh (100755), a symlink link-to-lf and an untracked notes-untracked.txt; writes a 4-line Claude Code transcript for session 11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555 under $HOME/.claude/projects/<slug>/ with the line shape of tests/unit/lib/vault/materialize.test.ts line 19-21; writes passphrase.txt ("windows smoke fixture passphrase 42"); runs `npx --yes "$SUBJECT_TGZ" vault setup "$OUT/vault.git" --passphrase-file "$OUT/passphrase.txt"` and `vault save <session>` (must print "appended"), then `vault sync` so the list cache holds the record (save does not refresh it); writes fixture.json { sessionId, originBranch, expected: { "lf.txt", unpushedSubject, changedPaths } }.

items.title: Given a packed subject tarball in SUBJECT_TGZ, when make-fixture.sh runs on Linux with a fresh output dir, then it exits 0 and creates origin.git, vault.git, passphrase.txt and fixture.json there.
Given the fixture was built, when `vault list --json` runs with the fixture OVERDECK_HOME, then its output contains session id 11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555.
When `vault save` does not print "appended", then make-fixture.sh exits non-zero and prints the save output.
When make-fixture.sh runs, then it creates files only under OUT and preserves the runner user's real ~/.overdeck and ~/.claude unchanged.
Add the native Windows probe scripts/windows-smoke/probe.ps1

verify_commands: gh run view <windows-smoke run id> --log (job windows, both matrix legs)
expected_outputs: each leg uploads results-windows-<shell> containing one JSON file with every catalogue step id exactly once

narrative.Action: Implement PRD W2: a PowerShell 7 script with params -Env -Subject -Fixture -Out that clones the fixture origin.git into $env:RUNNER_TEMP\w\proj, then runs step ids 1a,1b,1c,1d,2a,2b,3a,3b,3c,3d,3e,3f,3g,4a,4b,4c,4d,4e,4f,5a exactly as the PRD "Step catalogue" table defines (5a emitted as not-run with note "native env"), via an Invoke-Step helper that wraps each step in try/catch, captures combined output (last 4000 chars), exit code and status (pass|fail|partial|not-run). 1c starts `serve --port 3011` with Start-Process and OVERDECK_INTERNAL_TOKEN set, polls 90 s; 2b POSTs /api/conversations with Origin http://localhost:3011 and x-overdeck-internal-token; after 2b kill the server tree with taskkill /T /F. 3e follows checkpoint CP-2 (two claude --resume runs, compare outputs). Writes the Results JSON schema from the PRD as UTF-8 without BOM.

items.title: When a step throws or exits non-zero, then the probe records it as fail with its verbatim output and still runs every later step.
The probe produces a results file that contains each step id from the PRD step catalogue exactly once, with status one of pass, fail, partial or not-run.
Step 2b sends the Origin and x-overdeck-internal-token headers, so its recorded response is never the validateOrigin 403.
Step 3e records both `claude --resume` outputs (materialized id and the all-zero UUID) and applies the CP-2 rule for pass versus partial.
The probe emits the runner, node and git versions and the subject tarball name in the top-level JSON fields.
Add the WSL probe scripts/windows-smoke/probe-wsl.sh

verify_commands: gh run view <windows-smoke run id> --log (job wsl)
expected_outputs: the wsl job uploads results-wsl2 (or results-wsl1-fallback) with every step id exactly once

narrative.Action: Implement PRD W3: a bash script run inside the Ubuntu-24.04 WSL distro that installs Node 22 into ~/node and `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` (needed by 3e/3g), copies the fixture from /mnt/<drive> into ~/fx, clones origin.git to ~/w/proj, runs step ids 3a-4f with the same semantics as the Windows probe but with Linux paths, embeds the wsl status file passed as --wsl-status as the evidence of step 5a, emits 1a-2b as not-run with note "dashboard not in scope for WSL row", and writes the Results JSON (built with node -e for escaping) to the /mnt path given by --out. A `step` function with set +e inside ensures a failure never aborts later steps.

items.title: When run inside WSL with the fixture and subject tarball, then it writes a results file whose env is wsl2 (or wsl1-fallback when passed --env wsl1-fallback) with every catalogue step id exactly once.
The WSL results file records steps 1a through 2b as not-run with the note "dashboard not in scope for WSL row".
When a step fails, then the script records fail with verbatim evidence and continues with the next step.
When the WSL probe runs the B-flow, then its cwd is the Linux-filesystem path ~/w/proj, never a /mnt/c path.
Add the results summarizer scripts/windows-smoke/summarize.mjs with a unit test

expected_outputs: lint and typecheck complete without errors

narrative.Action: Implement PRD W4: a dependency-free Node ESM script exporting renderTable(results) and, when run as main, reading every *.json in the given dir and printing markdown: a header (run URL from GITHUB_SERVER_URL/GITHUB_REPOSITORY/GITHUB_RUN_ID when set, subject, per-env runner/node/git), the table (rows = step ids with short titles, columns in order windows-pwsh, windows-gitbash, wsl2 then any other env; cells "✅ pass", "❌ fail: <first evidence line ≤120 chars, | escaped>", "⚠️ partial: <note>", "— not-run", "missing"), then "## Details" with a <details> block per non-pass cell holding command, exit code and fenced verbatim evidence. Add the unit test named in files_scope.

items.title: Given a results object with a fail whose evidence contains "|", when renderTable runs, then the cell text contains "\|" and the table keeps one column per env.
Given a results file missing step 3c, when renderTable runs, then the 3c cell for that env renders "missing".
Given a pass and a fail, when renderTable runs, then only the fail produces a <details> block containing its verbatim evidence.
Add the windows-smoke GitHub Actions workflow

expected_outputs: a windows-smoke run appears for the branch push

narrative.Action: Implement PRD W5: .github/workflows/windows-smoke.yml with triggers workflow_dispatch and push (paths: the workflow file and scripts/windows-smoke/**), permissions contents: read, and jobs pack (ubuntu-latest: setup-node 22, setup-bun, bun install --frozen-lockfile, bun run build, CP-1 tarball check `tar tzf | grep dist/dashboard/server.js`, npm pack --ignore-scripts, upload "subject"), fixture (needs pack; make-fixture.sh; upload origin.git, vault.git, passphrase.txt, fixture.json as "fixture"), windows (windows-2022, needs pack+fixture, matrix shell [pwsh, gitbash], fail-fast false, npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code, probe with continue-on-error, upload results-windows-<shell>), wsl (windows-2022, Vampire/setup-wsl@v7 Ubuntu-24.04 wsl-version 2, record wsl --status and wsl -l -v, CP-3 fallback to wsl-version 1 with env wsl1-fallback, run probe-wsl.sh, upload results-wsl2), summary (ubuntu-latest, needs windows+wsl, if: always(), summarize.mjs to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and artifact windows-smoke-table). timeout-minutes: pack 20, fixture 10, windows 25, wsl 30, summary 5. Actions: checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, setup-bun@v2, upload/download-artifact@v4.

items.title: When the workflow file is read, then it contains triggers workflow_dispatch and on push only when the workflow file or scripts/windows-smoke/** changes; it is not referenced from ci.yml.
The workflow contains timeout-minutes on every job, and the windows matrix runs both pwsh and gitbash legs with fail-fast false.
The summary job runs with if: always() and uploads an artifact named windows-smoke-table even when a probe job fails.
The pack job fails before upload when the tarball lacks package/dist/dashboard/server.js.
Run windows-smoke and post the results table on #4331

expected_outputs: a #4331 comment contains the results table and a windows-smoke run URL
the PRD contains a ## Results section with the same table

narrative.Action: Implement PRD W6: push the branch (hazard H-1 fallback for workflow-scope rejection), wait for the whole windows-smoke run with one `gh run watch <id> --exit-status`, fix and re-push only harness errors (a job that fails before its probe writes results), then download windows-smoke-table, post it with `gh issue comment 4331 --body-file`, and append it to .pan/drafts/PAN-4331.md as "## Results (run <id>, <sha>)". The tracked PRD may be .pan/drafts/pan-4331.md or .pan/drafts/PAN-4331.md after promotion: edit the file `git ls-files .pan/drafts | grep -i 'pan-4331.md'` prints and never create the other case. Runs triggered before all five harness items are pushed are expected to fail; only a run on a commit containing all five counts.

items.title: A windows-smoke run for the branch produces all five job results, and its windows-smoke-table artifact contains columns for windows-pwsh, windows-gitbash and wsl2 (or wsl1-fallback).
Issue #4331 shows a comment that contains the table and the run URL, and every non-pass cell in it carries a verbatim error.
The tracked PRD draft for PAN-4331 contains a "## Results" section naming the run id and subject commit with the same table.
File one issue per blocking failure and link them on #4331

verify_commands: gh search issues "Found by PAN-4331" --repo eltmon/overdeck
expected_outputs: a #4331 comment lists every filed blocker as "- #<n> — step <id> (<envs>)" or states none were blocking

narrative.Action: Implement PRD W7: apply the FR-7 blocking definition (fail in 1c, 3a, 3b, 3c, 3d, 3g, 4a, 4b, 4c in any env — 5a is NOT blocking because a WSL2 start failure on a hosted runner is a GitHub environment limit — plus 2b when the error does not name the missing Herdr backend and its fix) to the results; group failures with one root cause across envs; for each, `gh issue create --repo eltmon/overdeck` with the body shape in W7 (Found by PAN-4331 + run URL, Part of PAN-2350, envs, command, exact error fenced, suspected code location, ## Acceptance criteria with "windows-smoke shows step <id> as pass"). Comment on #4331 with the list; append the same list under the PRD Results section. The tracked PRD may be .pan/drafts/pan-4331.md or .pan/drafts/PAN-4331.md after promotion: edit the file `git ls-files .pan/drafts | grep -i 'pan-4331.md'` prints and never create the other case.

items.title: Each distinct FR-7 blocking root cause produces exactly one new issue whose body contains "Found by PAN-4331", the exact error in a fenced block and an ## Acceptance criteria section.
Issue #4331 shows a comment that contains every filed issue as "- #<n> — step <id> (<envs>)", or stating that no step was blocking.
When failures share a root cause across environments, then W7 produces one issue that names all affected environments.
Record the Windows outcome in PAN-3762 NFR-9

expected_outputs: a #3762 comment carries the same outcome sentence

narrative.Action: Implement PRD W8: in .pan/drafts/pan-3762.md, on the line starting "- **NFR-9 — Platform scope.**", keep the existing text and append one sentence naming which Windows paths continue a vault conversation per the run (native standalone, WSL2, both or neither), with the run link and blocker issue numbers. Post the same sentence with `gh issue comment 3762`. Renumber nothing.

items.title: The NFR-9 line in .pan/drafts/pan-3762.md preserves its original text and contains a sentence that names PAN-4331, the verified Windows path(s) and the run link.
Issue #3762 shows a comment that contains the same sentence.
Add the verified Windows sections to the Session Vault docs

expected_outputs: both files contain a ## Windows heading

narrative.Action: Implement PRD W9: append "## Windows" at the end of docs/SESSION-VAULT.md and insert "## Windows" immediately before "## Where things live" in configuration/session-vault.mdx. Apply the W9 decision rule: native standalone is "supported" only if 3a, 3b, 3c, 3d, 4a, 4b, 4c pass in windows-pwsh ("supported with --no-launch" when only 3g fails, linking its issue); WSL2 is "supported" only if 5a and 3a-4c pass in wsl2; one sentence each for what 1c and 2b showed on the dashboard; name the exact environment (Windows Server 2022, GitHub windows-2022 runner, Node and Git versions), the date and run link; list observed 4d-4f line-ending/exec-bit/symlink behavior; mention Windows 11 and dual-boot only as not verified.

items.title: Each of docs/SESSION-VAULT.md and configuration/session-vault.mdx contains a "## Windows" section that names the GitHub windows-2022 runner with Node and Git versions and links the run.
Each Windows section contains native standalone and WSL2 support exactly as the W9 decision rule yields from the Results table, and links every filed blocker issue it mentions.
Neither section contains a claim of Windows 11 or dual-boot support; both describe them as not verified.
Each Windows section contains the observed line-ending, exec-bit and symlink results from steps 4d, 4e and 4f.
